content.comment_body: Hello, I read your suggestion about representing each day as a bit (such as 27.0, 27.1, etc.). Could you advise on how to handle hour and minute entries as well? I understand that the weekly timer uses VW format. What is the correct addressing format for specifying hours and minutes? Thank you.

Hi [user_name], I've attached an example using a [product_name] project and an LSC file. The project file is for the older version of [product_name] Web Editor [version_no], and the LSC file corresponds to [product_name] version [version_no]. Both the on and off times are stored in BCD format, which is why the block format in the editor is hexadecimal. For detailed configuration, check the Parameter-VM-Mapping in the LSC file.

Hello, thanks for your reply. I'm aiming to connect my [product_name] to another display, so I need to input hour and minute values from a third-party display. As you described, the weekday addressing format (for example, VM Mapping address VB28: SUN - 28.0, MON - 28.1, etc.) is clear. Since the weekly timer uses word format, I need to know the specific addressing format for entering hours and minutes.

1.) Your question concerns [product_name] Web Editor. However, it's not clear that you want to display and modify the weekly timer using an HMI; creating a dedicated topic would clarify this. 2.) I've shared that the switch-on and switch-off times use BCD coding for formatting.
Hello, I apologize for any confusion—I thought the topic was similar, so I commented here. I will create a new post addressing my specific question.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centered on obtaining technical information for configuring hour and minute values in a weekly timer for integration with third-party displays. Community responses explained that these values utilize BCD-coded formatting and pointed to example files and parameter mappings for reference. Some miscommunication highlighted a need for clearer documentation on data formats and addressing conventions when integrating external hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for thorough and clear documentation on addressing formats and data conventions for specifying hours and minutes, which would help in connecting [product_name] systems to external hardware more easily.
